title: Git Flow & Branching Strategy
description: Set up a complete Git Flow branching strategy with feature branches, release branches, and hotfix workflows.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Implement a production-grade Git Flow branching strategy in a sample repository. Create proper branch naming conventions, merge strategies, and release workflows that a team can adopt immediately.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Git 2.x
- Pre-created bare repository at /opt/gitflow-repo.git
- Clone URL: /opt/gitflow-repo.git
- Working directory: /opt/gitflow-lab

### Tasks
1. Clone the bare repository and configure Git user as 'lab-admin'
2. Create a main branch as the production-ready branch
3. Create a develop branch from main for integration
4. Create a feature branch named 'feature/user-auth' from develop
5. Add a simple auth.js file, commit, and merge back to develop via --no-ff
6. Create a release branch 'release/v1.0.0' from develop
7. Create a hotfix branch 'hotfix/critical-fix' from main
8. Merge hotfix to both main and develop

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Git pre-installed
- All operations on local bare repo

Create a main branch as the production-ready branch
Create a develop branch from main for integration
Create a feature branch named 'feature/user-auth' from develop
Add a simple auth.js file, commit, and merge back to develop via --no-ff
Create a release branch 'release/v1.0.0' from develop
Create a hotfix branch 'hotfix/critical-fix' from main
Merge hotfix to both main and develop

title: CI/CD Pipeline with GitHub Actions
description: Build a complete CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions with build, test, security scan, and deploy stages.
briefing:

title: TDD: Build Feature with Tests First
description: Implement a REST API feature using Test-Driven Development with the Red-Green-Refactor cycle.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Build a complete shopping cart API feature using strict TDD methodology. Write tests first (Red), implement minimal code to pass (Green), then refactor for quality (Refactor). Document the TDD cycle at each step.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Node.js 20
- Jest pre-installed for testing
- Working directory: /opt/tdd-lab
- Starter project in /opt/tdd-lab/cart-api/

### Tasks
1. Write failing tests for adding items to cart (Red phase)
2. Implement minimal code to pass tests (Green phase)
3. Refactor the code and ensure tests still pass
4. Write failing tests for removing items from cart
5. Implement remove functionality and refactor
6. Write failing tests for calculating totals with discounts
7. Implement discount logic and refactor
8. Write integration tests combining all features

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Node.js 20 and Jest pre-installed
- TDD cycle documentation in README.md

title: Design Patterns: Factory, Strategy, Observer
description: Implement Factory, Strategy, and Observer design patterns in a real-world e-commerce discount system.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Implement three classic design patterns — Factory, Strategy, and Observer — in a discount calculation system for an e-commerce platform. Each pattern should solve a distinct problem in the system.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Node.js 20
- Jest for testing
- Working directory: /opt/design-patterns-lab
- Starter project in /opt/design-patterns-lab/src/

### Tasks
1. Implement a DiscountFactory that creates discount objects by type
2. Create concrete discount strategies: PercentageOff, FixedAmount, BuyXGetYFree
3. Implement a DiscountStrategy interface with calculate() method
4. Create an EventEmitter-based DiscountObserver for logging
5. Add a DiscountApplied event that triggers on discount application
6. Create a DiscountManager that coordinates Factory, Strategy, and Observer
7. Write unit tests verifying each pattern works correctly
8. Create an integration test using all three patterns together

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Node.js 20 and Jest pre-installed
- Source code structure provided in starter project

title: Refactoring Legacy Code

briefing:

3. Create a Service layer with business logic
4. Refactor controllers to use dependency injection
5. Add error handling middleware
6. Create configuration management module
7. Ensure all existing tests still pass
8. Add new tests for the refactored services

- Node.js 20, Jest, ESLint pre-installed

title: Documentation-Driven Development
description: Practice documentation-first development by writing OpenAPI specs, ADRs, and README docs before implementation.
briefing:

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Node.js 20

8. Validate the OpenAPI spec using a linter

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Node.js 20 pre-installed

title: Feature Flags Implementation

briefing:

4. Add user targeting rules (email, region, plan)

6. Set up Redis caching for flag evaluations
7. Add webhook notifications when flags change
8. Create an admin dashboard for flag management

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Node.js 20, Redis, and MongoDB available
- Pre-configured Docker Compose stack

title: Canary Deployments with Feature Toggles
description: Implement canary deployment strategy with traffic splitting and automated rollback on error thresholds.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Implement a canary deployment system that gradually shifts traffic between old and new versions. Monitor error rates and automatically rollback if thresholds are exceeded.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Docker and Docker Compose
- Nginx for traffic splitting
- Working directory: /opt/canary-deploy

### Tasks
1. Create two versions of a simple Node.js application (v1 and v2)
2. Set up Nginx as a load balancer with weighted routing
3. Create a deployment script that manages traffic split percentages
4. Add health check endpoints to both application versions
5. Create a monitoring script that checks error rates
6. Implement automated rollback when error rate > 5%
7. Create a canary deployment pipeline script
8. Test the full canary deployment and rollback flow

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root with Docker socket
- Nginx, Node.js 20 available
- All scripts must be executable

title: Technical Debt Tracking Dashboard
description: Build a dashboard that tracks code complexity, test coverage, dependency health, and code smells.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Create a technical debt tracking dashboard that aggregates metrics from code analysis tools. Track code complexity, test coverage trends, dependency vulnerabilities, and code smells over time.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Node.js 20
- ESLint, npm-audit, and complexity tools pre-installed
- Working directory: /opt/tech-debt-lab
- Sample Node.js project at /opt/tech-debt-lab/target-project/

### Tasks
1. Create a metrics collection script that runs ESLint analysis
2. Add code complexity analysis using plato or cr
3. Create a test coverage history tracker
4. Add dependency vulnerability scanning with npm audit
5. Create a JSON report generator for all metrics
6. Build an HTML dashboard to visualize debt metrics
7. Set up a cron-like script for periodic metric collection
8. Create alerts for when metrics exceed thresholds

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- Node.js 20 and analysis tools pre-installed
- Target project provided for analysis
